answers.assumptions: That the Oct 8 support would hold and that 'oversold' meant a bounce was near. Oversold can stay oversold when the whole crypto market is falling (inflation worries, Fed hike talk).
answers.change_strategy: Prefer reward:risk of 2 or more for crypto bounce trades, because the 1.5 minimum leaves little room. Put the stop a bit further from noisy support levels, or skip the trade if that makes reward:risk too small.
answers.evidence: Kraken daily candles (support lows Oct 8 and Sep 20), RSI computed from those closes, The Block and CoinDesk news. Reward:risk was only about 1.6, just over the 1.5 minimum.
answers.hypothesis: Solana was oversold (RSI about 28) just above real support at 150.2-150.5 CAD, so a bounce toward the 165.82 breakdown level was plausible.
answers.process_luck_mistake: Mostly sound process with bad luck: the plan had a clear exit rule and it was followed. One process gap: about 26 hours with no runs meant the exit happened a day late, but the late exit price (149.34) was close to the planned stop, so the gap cost little here.
answers.rules_followed: Yes: position size about 100 CAD, stop set below real support, and exit on the written invalidation rule. The stop only fires when a run is active, which is a weakness.
answers.test_next_time: Check whether buying 'oversold near support' works better when the bigger trend (20-day average) is also turning up, not falling.
answers.what_happened: No bounce. Solana kept sliding: intraday 145.24 on Oct 13, a daily close of 148.27 on Oct 14 (below the 148.71 line) and an intraday low of 142.93 on Oct 15. Sold at about 149.34 for a loss of 4.58 CAD (-4.6%).

lessons: Oversold is not the same as about to bounce, especially when the whole market is falling.
A stop only protects you if something is watching the price; missed runs make stops late.

mistakes.description: Bought while the 20-day trend was still pointing down; the bounce idea was early.

original_thesis: Solana fell fast to just above real support (150.2-150.5 CAD, Oct 8 and Sep 20 lows) and is oversold (RSI about 28); a bounce back toward the 165.82 breakdown level is plausible.
